messages.subject: ODBC error
messages.body_plain: I am trying to use the RODBC library within rApache to connect to a MS SQL server using unixODBC and FreeTDS.  I have everything set up correctly and can succesfully connect to and execute queries against the database using isql.  I can also load R as root and run commands with RODBC without error.  However, when trying to run in rApache, it cannot connect to the database.  I get the errors "[unixODBC][FreeTDS][SQL Server]Unable to connect: Adaptive Server is unavailable or does not exist" and "Unable to connect to data source" in the apache error log.  Can anyone offer any advice why these would only fail in rApache?  Thanks!

Well I had a chance to release a new version of rApache today. I found what I thought was a pretty critical bug over the weekend while migrating a server here at vandy. Decided to fix the content-type thingy too. Please let me know how it runs for you.

Jeff

Download from:

http://www.rapache.net/downloads.html

Changelog Entry:

2012-10-01 jeffreyhorner <jeffrey.horner@XXXXXXX>

* Release 1.2.1
* Don't parse POST paylod if apreq2 doesn't have a parser for the
given content type.

* More R protections>

* Allow RFileHandlers to share environments if the handlers are
defined in the same file.

messages.subject: Re: rApache and a Web Console
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

to run R commands in a browser, you could setup a non-interactive console with even a simple textarea or you may look for a nifty JS library. This can be addressed quite easily I suppose.

But you should be familiar with securing/hardening your newly installed system, and take this serious :)
I really suggest you to check out e.g. RApparmor <https://github.com/jeroenooms/RAppArmor> and sandboxR <https://github.com/Rapporter/sandboxR> packages. I have created a simple webapp for the latter, you might be interested: http://sandboxr.no-ip.org/

Best,
Gergely

Unless you want to do that for commercial purposes, I'd rather drop a few lines of jQuery to hit OpenCPU HTTP API via CORS/JSONP and return output in an user-friendly format. Rolling your own interface will be pain in the @$$, or a good practice, depending on your needs/skill level.

See docs for details: https://public.opencpu.org/pages/docs.html

Otherwise, RApparmor, sandboxR, just like Gergely suggested... oh, and... good luck! =)

OR, something like this even: http://code.google.com/p/renjin/

aL3xa
